intro: Retention rate is the share of your existing customers who were still customers at the end of the period. Enter the customer counts below to get both retention and churn.

sections.heading: What retention rate measures
sections.body: Retention rate is (customers at period end − customers acquired during the period) ÷ customers at period start. Subtracting new customers matters — without it, new signups would mask churn among the customers you already had, which is the number this metric is actually trying to isolate.

sections.heading: The formula, and its complement
sections.body: Starting with 1,000 customers, ending the period with 1,050, and having acquired 150 new ones during it: (1,050 − 150) ÷ 1,000 = 90% retention. Churn rate is reported as 1 − retention, so this same period has a 10% churn rate. That relationship only holds because both numbers are measured over the exact same population and the exact same time window — a churn rate calculated over a different period, or a different customer segment, isn't the complement of this retention rate anymore, it's a different measurement entirely.

sections.heading: Reading the number
sections.body: Retention rate is a period-level average — it tells you how a whole cohort of existing customers behaved over one stretch of time, not what happens to any individual customer or how retention trends across the customer's actual lifetime. For that finer-grained view, cohort retention (like D1/D7/D30 retention in mobile) tracks the same group from a shared starting point instead of a rolling period, and answers a related but different question: not 'how many of my current customers stuck around this month,' but 'how many of the people who signed up on day zero are still here N days later.'

sections.heading: Common mistakes
items: Forgetting to subtract new customers from the end count, which inflates retention by counting brand-new signups as 'retained.'
Comparing retention rates calculated over different period lengths (a month vs. a quarter) as if they were the same measurement.
